title: Amritsar vs Varanasi: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Amritsar for accessible spirituality and world-class food. Varanasi for raw, ancient India that will change how you see life and death.

categories.name: Signature Landmark
categories.summary: Golden Temple vs Ganges ghats — both are world-class spiritual experiences but hit very differently.

categories.name: Food & Dining
categories.summary: Amritsar is one of India's greatest food cities. Punjab street food — dal makhani, kulcha, amritsari fish — wins by a wide margin.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Varanasi is slightly cheaper, especially for ghat-side accommodation. Both cities are excellent budget value.

categories.name: Photography
categories.summary: Dawn ghat scenes, the Ganga Aarti ceremony, and atmospheric old city alleys give Varanasi the photography edge.

categories.name: Ease for First-Timers
categories.summary: Amritsar is more organized and welcoming. Varanasi's sensory intensity can overwhelm first-time India visitors.

categories.name: Safety
categories.summary: Amritsar is notably safer with fewer touts. Varanasi is safe but requires more vigilance.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Sarnath + Bodhgaya give Varanasi strong day trip options. Amritsar's Wagah Border is unique but narrower overall.

categories.name: Evening Atmosphere
categories.summary: The Ganga Aarti ceremony is one of India's most visually extraordinary events. Amritsar's evening Golden Temple is serene but calmer.

faq.question: Is Amritsar or Varanasi better for a first-time India trip?
faq.answer: Amritsar is the gentler introduction. The Golden Temple is world-class and the city is more organized. Varanasi rewards experienced India travelers.
